input.strategy_title: Integrated GenAI model evaluation for RHOAI
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers adopting generative models on RHOAI have no supported way to answer
"is this model good enough for my use case?" inside the platform. Evaluation
today happens in ad-hoc notebooks with lm-evaluation-harness or vendor tools,
results live in spreadsheets, and nothing links an evaluation to the model
version that was actually deployed. We need a first-class evaluation capability:
run standard and custom benchmarks against models served on the platform,
persist results alongside the model version, and let users compare candidates
before promoting one to production.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1  | P0 | Users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite. |
| HLR-2  | P0 | Standard benchmark suites (e.g. MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag exposed through lm-eval task names) are available out of the box. |
| HLR-3  | P0 | Evaluation results are persisted and linked to the Model Registry version of the evaluated model. |
| HLR-4  | P1 | Users can define custom evaluation tasks (own datasets and metrics) and run them through the same flow. |
| HLR-5  | P1 | The Dashboard shows evaluation runs, their status, and per-benchmark scores, and allows side-by-side comparison of two model versions. |
| HLR-6  | P1 | Evaluations can be embedded as a step in a Data Science Pipeline so promotion flows can gate on scores. |
| HLR-7  | P1 | Llama Stack's eval provider API is backed by the platform evaluation service, so agents/apps built on Llama Stack get the same results. |
| HLR-8  | P2 | Evaluation runs record cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) for capacity planning. |
| HLR-9  | P2 | Product documentation covers the evaluation workflow end to end, including custom task authoring. |

## Affected Components

- TrustyAI
- Llama Stack
- Dashboard
- Data Science Pipelines
- Model Registry

## Out of Scope

- Human-preference (arena style) evaluation collection
- Automatic model promotion decisions — pipelines gate, humans promote
- Fine-tuning feedback loops driven by evaluation scores

## Open Questions

1. Execution engine: TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview) already wraps
   lm-evaluation-harness — do we build on it as the single execution path, or is
   a new evaluation service needed to also serve Llama Stack's eval provider
   API? Needs a technical investigation with a recommendation.
2. Result schema: what is the canonical result format persisted to Model
   Registry custom properties, and does it survive benchmark-suite version
   bumps? Prototype against real MMLU output before committing.
3. Benchmark dataset licensing: which standard suites can we redistribute in
   disconnected environments, and which must be fetched by the customer?

# Extend TrustyAI LMEvalJob as the single evaluation execution path

*Conditional branch epic — instantiated only if the execution-engine
investigation recommends Outcome A (build on LMEvalJob).*

## Description

Implement the platform's evaluation execution capability by extending TrustyAI's
existing LMEvalJob integration (which wraps EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness)
into the single execution path: users can launch an evaluation of a model served
on the platform (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected
benchmark suite, and the same path serves Llama Stack's eval provider API.

## Scope

- Extend the LMEvalJob CRD / job runner so an evaluation targets a served model
  (KServe InferenceService endpoint or LlamaStackDistribution endpoint), not
  only raw endpoints.
- Support launching an evaluation against a selected benchmark suite (standard
  lm-eval task names and, later, custom task definitions).
- Expose evaluation run lifecycle (launch, running, succeeded/failed) and
  per-benchmark results through an interface the Dashboard, Data Science
  Pipelines step, and Llama Stack eval provider can build against.
- Emit evaluation results (and cost/duration metadata: tokens, wall-clock, GPU
  time where available) at a well-defined capture point so they can be
  persisted against the evaluated model's registered version.
- Address Tech Preview gaps identified by the investigation for production use
  (error handling, project scoping, run limits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can launch an evaluation of a model served via a KServe endpoint
  against a selected benchmark suite, and the run reaches a terminal status.
- A user can launch the same evaluation against a model served via a Llama
  Stack distribution.
- Evaluation run status and per-benchmark scores are observable through the
  exposed interface while and after the run executes.
- Each completed run records cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU
  time) alongside its scores.
- Results are emitted in the canonical result format recommended by the result
  schema prototype, at a documented capture point.
- Rollback/safety: extending the existing LMEvalJob path must not regress the
  current Tech Preview behavior (existing LMEvalJob usages keep working).
- Build pipeline green for trustyai-service-operator changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): launch an evaluation of a served model against a selected
  benchmark suite.
- HLR-8 (P2): runs record cost/duration metadata (execution/recording half;
  persistence is covered by the Model Registry persistence work).

Implement the platform's evaluation execution capability as a new evaluation
service: users can launch an evaluation of a model served on the platform (KServe
endpoint or Llama Stack distribution) against a selected benchmark suite, and
the service also backs Llama Stack's eval provider API so agents and apps built
on Llama Stack get the same results.

## Scope

- Design and implement the evaluation service (execution API, run lifecycle
  management, project-scoped multi-tenancy) per the architecture recommended by
  the execution-engine investigation.
- Execute evaluations by orchestrating lm-evaluation-harness runs against
  served models (KServe InferenceService endpoints and LlamaStackDistribution
  endpoints), supporting standard lm-eval task names and, later, custom task
  definitions.
- Expose run lifecycle (launch, running, succeeded/failed) and per-benchmark
  results through interfaces the Dashboard, Data Science Pipelines step, and
  Llama Stack eval provider build against.
- Implement the Llama Stack eval provider adapter surface so the service can
  serve as the distribution's eval provider.
- Emit evaluation results (and cost/duration metadata: tokens, wall-clock, GPU
  time where available) at a well-defined capture point so they can be persisted
  against the evaluated model's registered version.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can launch an evaluation of a model served via a KServe endpoint
  against a selected benchmark suite, and the run reaches a terminal status.
- A user can launch the same evaluation against a model served via a Llama
  Stack distribution.
- Evaluation run status and per-benchmark scores are observable through the
  exposed interface while and after the run executes.
- The service can act as the backing implementation for Llama Stack's eval
  provider API.
- Each completed run records cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU
  time) alongside its scores.
- Results are emitted in the canonical result format recommended by the result
  schema prototype, at a documented capture point.
- The new service is deployable per-project through the platform operator
  surface consistent with other RHOAI components.
- Build pipeline green for the new service's repository.

  benchmark suite.

# Evaluation execution engine investigation (LMEvalJob vs new service)

## Description

Resolve the strategy's first open question: should the platform build on
TrustyAI's LMEvalJob (Tech Preview, wrapping EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness)
as the single evaluation execution path, or is a new evaluation service needed
that can also serve Llama Stack's eval provider API? Produce a technical
investigation with a recommendation that determines the shape of all downstream
execution and integration work.

## Scope

- Analyze the LMEvalJob CRD and its job runner in trustyai-service-operator
  (upstream and midstream): current capabilities, extensibility, maturity gaps
  as a Tech Preview, and GA-readiness.
- Analyze Llama Stack's eval provider API surface (upstream meta-llama/llama-stack
  and the opendatahub-io distribution) and determine what a backing
  implementation must provide.
- Determine whether LMEvalJob can be extended to serve both the
  Dashboard-launched evaluation flow and the Llama Stack eval provider API, or
  whether a separate evaluation service is architecturally required.
- Evaluate implications for each option: KServe endpoint and Llama Stack
  distribution as evaluation targets, result emission interfaces, multi-tenant
  project scoping, and operational footprint.
- Deliver a written recommendation with the decision criteria and evidence,
  selecting between two bounded outcomes:
  - **Outcome A**: extend TrustyAI LMEvalJob as the single execution path.
  - **Outcome B**: build a new platform evaluation service.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The investigation report documents LMEvalJob's current capabilities and
  limitations as an execution engine for standard and custom lm-eval tasks,
  with evidence from the operator source and CRD definitions.
- The report documents the Llama Stack eval provider API contract and states
  explicitly whether LMEvalJob can back it directly, can be extended to back
  it, or cannot back it.
- A single recommendation (Outcome A or Outcome B) is made with decision
  criteria, covering impact on the execution flow, result persistence capture
  point, and the Llama Stack provider integration.
- The recommendation identifies which downstream work changes under the
  non-chosen outcome, so downstream plans can be adjusted without re-analysis.

## HLR Traceability

- Gates HLR-1 (P0), and transitively HLR-2, HLR-3, HLR-4, HLR-5, HLR-6, HLR-7:
  the execution engine decision determines what the evaluation launch
  capability, suite delivery, result capture, Dashboard surface, pipeline step,
  custom task flow, and Llama Stack provider all build against.

# Evaluation result schema prototype (Model Registry custom properties)

## Description

Resolve the strategy's second open question: what is the canonical evaluation
result format persisted to Model Registry custom properties, and does it survive
benchmark-suite version bumps? The strategy requires a prototype against real
MMLU output before committing to a schema. This investigation produces that
prototype and the recommended canonical schema.

## Scope

- Run real lm-evaluation-harness evaluations (starting with MMLU) and capture
  representative raw result output.
- Design a canonical result schema that fits Model Registry custom properties
  on ModelVersion entities (types and size constraints of the custom-properties
  extension point per the Model Registry REST API / OpenAPI spec).
- Validate that the schema represents per-benchmark scores, benchmark-suite
  versions, and evaluation run metadata (including cost/duration fields:
  tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) without breaking on benchmark-suite version
  bumps.
- Determine how an evaluation result is linked to the exact registered model
  version that was deployed and evaluated, using the registry's existing
  model-version-to-serving-deployment linkage.
- Deliver the prototyped schema, populated examples from real MMLU output, and
  a recommendation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A prototype maps real MMLU evaluation output into Model Registry custom
  properties on a ModelVersion, retrievable via the Model Registry REST API.
- The proposed schema records the benchmark-suite identity and version, so a
  suite version bump does not invalidate or corrupt previously stored results.
- The schema accommodates per-benchmark scores plus cost/duration metadata
  (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time).
- The report demonstrates how a stored result is resolved back to the evaluated
  model version, including the served-endpoint-to-registered-version linkage.
- The recommendation is concrete enough that the persistence implementation can
  proceed without further schema design work.

## HLR Traceability

- Gates HLR-3 (P0): results persisted and linked to the Model Registry version
  of the evaluated model.
- Gates the persistence half of HLR-8 (P2): cost/duration metadata is part of
  the schema under design.

# Benchmark dataset licensing investigation

## Description

Resolve the strategy's third open question: which standard benchmark suites can
be redistributed by the platform in disconnected environments, and which must be
fetched by the customer? The answer determines the delivery mechanism for the
out-of-the-box benchmark suite capability.

## Scope

- Enumerate the candidate standard suites exposed through lm-eval task names
  (starting with MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag) and the datasets they load.
- For each suite/dataset, determine the license and its redistribution terms
  (redistributable in a product image vs must be fetched by the customer),
  citing the authoritative license text.
- Produce a categorized list: platform-redistributable vs customer-fetch, with
  license references.
- Identify the customer-fetch mechanism implications for disconnected
  environments (air-gapped clusters) for the non-redistributable suites, and
  recommend a delivery approach per category.
- Flag any suite where redistribution status is unclear and needs legal review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every candidate standard suite is listed with its dataset license(s) and a
  redistribution classification (redistributable / customer-fetch / needs legal
  review).
- Each classification cites the license text or terms it is based on.
- For customer-fetch suites, the report describes how a customer in a
  disconnected environment obtains and supplies the dataset.
- Any items requiring legal sign-off are explicitly flagged with the specific
  question legal must answer.

## HLR Traceability

- Gates HLR-2 (P0): standard benchmark suites available out of the box — the
  licensing outcome decides whether "out of the box" means bundled
  redistribution or a guided fetch mechanism.

# Persist evaluation results linked to Model Registry model versions

## Description

Implement persistence of evaluation results: every completed evaluation run's
per-benchmark scores and metadata are stored against the Model Registry version
of the evaluated model, using the canonical result schema prototyped against
real MMLU output, so results live alongside the model version rather than in
spreadsheets.

## Scope

- Implement writing of evaluation results to Model Registry custom properties
  on the evaluated model's ModelVersion, using the canonical schema recommended
  by the result-schema prototype (per-benchmark scores, benchmark-suite
  identity and version, run metadata).
- Resolve the evaluated model's registered version from the served endpoint
  that was evaluated (KServe endpoint or Llama Stack distribution), using the
  registry's model-version-to-serving-deployment linkage.
- Persist cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) recorded by the
  evaluation execution capability.
- Read path: stored results are retrievable via the Model Registry REST API so
  downstream consumers (Dashboard comparison views, promotion-gating pipeline
  steps) can query them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After an evaluation run completes, its per-benchmark scores are retrievable
  from the Model Registry REST API as custom properties on the evaluated
  model's ModelVersion.
- The stored result is linked to the exact model version that was deployed and
  evaluated, resolved from the served endpoint.
- Stored results record the benchmark-suite identity and version and remain
  readable after a benchmark-suite version bump (validated per the schema
  prototype).
- Cost/duration metadata (tokens, wall-clock, GPU time) is persisted with the
  result.
- Registry health: writing evaluation custom properties does not degrade
  Model Registry performance or existing registry UX (passive-component
  validation — the registry keeps working).
- Build pipeline green for affected repositories.

## HLR Traceability
